Comment “Bachatt” to automate your investment process and get ₹50 balance credited in your account 

I’ve recently done it and now 

Every single day, ₹301 gets automatically deducted from my bank account and invested through Bachatt into InstaFD.

I love this because I don’t have to actively think about investing every day. It just happens.

And it slowly builds my emergency fund, while also letting that money grow over the longer term. And because I can withdraw it whenever I need to, it gives me that flexibility too.

If I keep investing ₹301 every single day, assuming an 8% annual return, this is what it could look like:

1 month → ~₹9,030
3 months → ~₹27,356
6 months → ~₹55,883
1 year → ~₹1.14 lakh
3 years → ~₹3.72 lakh
10 years → ~₹16.83 lakh

So in 6 months, I’d have built a decent emergency cushion. And if I just keep going, that same ₹301 a day could grow into a much larger corpus over time.

It’s also a nice way to make sure those random ₹300-ish expenses don’t quietly eat up my money every day. 

You can start it with as little as ₹101 a day and let consistency do its thing.

Today hiring has a cat and mouse problem. Candidates are using AI to make their resumes and recruiters are using AI to screen resumes. But if done right, AI can make hiring more human. And we saw how that’s done via the new AI LinkedIn recruiter at the LI office in blr 📍

Not everything you can do with AI is worth doing with AI.

I ranked common AI use cases into four categories:

Life-changing: AI handles work that genuinely saves time or unlocks new capabilities.

Actually useful: AI helps you think, learn, or handle repetitive tasks without replacing your judgment.

Fake productivity: AI makes the work look faster while adding unnecessary steps or removing the thinking that actually matters.

Please do it yourself: Anything where the human part is the whole point — like dating, hiring decisions, or anything that requires real judgment.

The goal isn’t to use AI for everything.

It’s to use AI where it makes you better, faster, or more capable — and stay human where that’s the value.

AI has made polish cheap.

A great resume, deck, email or strategy document used to tell you something about the person behind it. Today, almost anyone can produce work that looks impressive.

Which means I’ve started trusting the output less and the follow-up questions more.

Can you explain why you made that decision?
Can you defend the assumption?
Can you think when the conversation goes somewhere you didn’t prepare for?

AI can improve the articulation of your thinking. It can even disguise weak thinking for a while.

But eventually, someone asks the next question.

And that’s where the difference shows.
